Sabtecha
SAB-teh-kah
n. (proper name; fifth son of Cush, son of Ham)
Hebrew Sabtecha, of uncertain meaning; 1 Chronicles 1:9 spells it the same while the neighbouring Sabtah appears as Sabta.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Sabtecha closes the list of Cush's sons: “And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha: and the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan” (Genesis 10:7), with the parallel at 1 Chronicles 1:9. Cush is the first-named son of Ham, and his line spreads into Africa and Arabia; Seba and Sheba and Dedan are names the prophets and the psalms use of distant trading peoples who will one day bring gifts to Zion. The Authorized Version uses Sabtecha twice and tells us nothing else about him. The dictionary notes what the surrounding names make of the list. Cush's line includes Nimrod, the first empire-builder, three verses later; it also includes the peoples of Psalm 72:10, “the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.” The same genealogy holds Babel and the nations who bring tribute to the Messiah. That is the shape of the whole Bible in one chapter: out of the families of the earth God raises both the tower and the worshippers.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Sabtecha is a proper name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Sabtecha is a Hebrew proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears at Genesis 10:7 and 1 Chronicles 1:9.

He is the fifth and last named son of Cush, the firstborn of Ham.

His brothers include Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, and Raamah.

Raamah's sons Sheba and Dedan are named in the same verse.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:7 — "And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha: and the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan."

1Ch 1:9 — "And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. And the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan."

Psa 72:10 — "The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts."

Modern Corruption

The genealogy of Ham has been abused to justify racial subjugation; Scripture gives no such warrant and the curse fell on Canaan.

expand to see more

The line of Ham has carried one of the ugliest misreadings in the history of interpretation. The curse of Genesis 9 fell on Canaan, not on Ham and not on Cush, and it was fulfilled in the Canaanite nations dispossessed under Joshua. It has never had anything to do with the peoples of Africa, and the use of this genealogy to justify enslaving them was wickedness built on a text that does not say it.

The principle to recover is Psalm 72:10. Cush's line is named among the peoples who bring gifts to the Messiah's throne, and the Ethiopian eunuch is reading Isaiah in Acts 8. In Christ there is neither Greek nor Jew, and the Table of Nations is a genealogy of one race, not a ranking of several.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Sabtecha, meaning uncertain; fifth son of Cush in the Hamite genealogy of Genesis 10.

expand to see more

Hebrew Sabtecha; the meaning is not recoverable with certainty.

Genesis 10:7 and 1 Chronicles 1:9 are the only occurrences.

Cush is the firstborn of Ham and the father of Nimrod.

Seba, Sheba, and Dedan in the same list are distant trading peoples.

Psalm 72:10 names Sheba and Seba as bringing gifts to the King.
